intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the CFAP47 gene (301057) on chromosome Xp21.1.

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the CFAP47 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: our experimental observations in humans and mice demonstrate that hemizygous mutations in CFAP47 can induce X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia
checks.explanation: The paper does not use the name SPGFX3, but the disorder it describes (X-linked MMAF/asthenoteratozoospermia with male infertility) is the same, so the claim is supported.

checks.claim: The CFAP47 gene is located on chromosome Xp21.1.
checks.evidence_quote: permitted the identification of a hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion removing the entire CFAP47 gene
checks.explanation: A deletion at Xp21.1 that removes the whole gene places CFAP47 at Xp21.1.

paragraphs.text: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) causes primary male infertility. Affected men have asthenoteratozoospermia, with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF) (Liu et al., 2021).

checks.claim: Men affected with SPGFX3 have multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF).
checks.evidence_quote: All men harboring hemizygous CFAP47 variants displayed typical MMAF phenotypes.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) reported 3 unrelated Chinese men who had primary infertility caused by asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF). They also reported an Australian man with severe asthenoteratozoospermia. The authors stated that all men who carried hemizygous CFAP47 variants had typical MMAF phenotypes.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) performed whole-exome sequencing in 3 unrelated Chinese men with MMAF. Each man carried a hemizygous missense variant in the X-linked CFAP47 gene (301057). None of the 3 variants was found in human control population genome databases, and multiple bioinformatic tools predicted all 3 to be deleterious. Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence showed obviously reduced CFAP47 levels in spermatozoa from all 3 men. CFAP47 encodes a cilia- and flagella-associated protein that is highly expressed in testis.

paragraphs.text: Liao et al. (2022) screened 7 men with MMAF and found 2 novel variants in the CFAP47 gene in one of them: c.706G-A (V236M) and c.1337C-T (T446M). Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence showed that CFAP47 was dramatically reduced in this man's sperm. WDR87 expression was also significantly reduced, with weak signals next to the sperm nuclei. The authors concluded that CFAP47 is needed to transport WDR87 during formation of the sperm flagellum.

paragraphs.text: Liao et al. (2022) found that WDR87 was highly expressed in human and mouse testis. In mice, WDR87 was located in the cytoplasm around the nucleus of spermatocytes and round spermatids. It moved to the manchette during spermiogenesis and ended up in the middle piece of the sperm tail. The authors identified CFAP47 as a protein that interacts with WDR87 in the sperm flagellar midpiece. They concluded that the 2 proteins form a complex involved in assembling the sperm tail.
